title: Redwood migration demo: OpenAI/Anthropic/Together parity mapping
summary: Demo focused on API and Console parity mapping for teams migrating from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood. Covered model name mapping, embeddings differences, function-calling/streaming behavior, security (SOC2, SAML, KMS), and pilot benchmarking plan. AE + SE to provide parity doc, quickstart repo, and run a 2-week benchmark pilot.

Customer to provide sample prompt set and traffic profile for benchmarks (by 2026-04-22)
Maya to run pilot benchmark and share results (kickoff 2026-04-27)
Jordan to send security pack and SOC2 artifacts (by 2026-04-21)

Elena Martinez - Share representative prompt set and 7-day traffic profile - due 2026-04-22
Maya Patel - Kick off benchmark pilot & collect latency/cost/quality results - start 2026-04-27

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-18 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (CTO - NovaHealth), Elena Martinez (Head of AI), Daniel Lee (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Procurement)

[00:00] Jordan Blake: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we know you had a lot of questions about migrating from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together over to Redwood so the plan for today is we, uh, will walk through API parity, the console, and our Optimize suggestions, and then leave time for security and pilot questions.

[00:12] Samir Rao: cool yeah thanks Jordan, we've been evaluating cost and latency. main concern is parity — will our existing calls just work or do we need to map things.

[00:20] Maya Patel: great question. at a high level we provide an API surface that's intentionally familiar — you can call text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking. we map popular model names to Redwood variants; i'll show an example mapping from gpt-like and anthropic-like names to our supported runtime. there are a few gotchas (tokenization and streaming differences) we'll call out.

[00:45] Elena Martinez: quick thing — function calling. a lot of our pipelines depend on structured function outputs. does Redwood do the same semantics as OpenAI's function-calling and Anthropic's tool-calling?

[00:52] Maya Patel: yes — we support function/tool calling and structured output. implementation differences: our JSON schema enforcement is stricter by default, but you can opt to relax it. streaming for function outputs is supported, though the chunking cadence can differ because of our batching/kv-cache optimizations. sometimes the transcriber may show "Redbend Console" instead of Redwood Console, sorry for the auto-audio glitch.

[01:17] Daniel Lee: when you say "batching/kv-cache" will that affect latency for interactive flows, like chat where we need <200ms tail latency for many queries?

[01:25] Maya Patel: good callout — for low tail-latency interactive traffic we recommend a configuration that prioritizes single-request hot paths: smaller batch windows, KV-cache pinning for conversational state, and dedicated instances or reserved capacity. for many customers that requires Dedicated or reserved pool; for occasional traffic hosted plan with smart routing is fine.

[01:45] Jordan Blake: and to add — we expose these knobs in the Console and via API params so you can tune per-route. the Optimize tab can suggest batching/caching profiles based on observed token distribution.

[02:00] Samir Rao: on embeddings — we currently use OpenAI text-embedding-3-large. how do embeddings map and what about vector dimension differences?

[02:08] Maya Patel: embeddings mapping is a big theme. we have curated embedding models that are compatible in vector-space for common tasks. sometimes dims differ — in that case we provide migration guidance: re-indexing vectors, or running a small model-compat transform. also we supply an embeddings performance profile (throughput/cost). we'll include an embeddings parity spreadsheet in the doc pack.

[02:35] Elena Martinez: tokenization — we've had subtle score shifts after moving models because punctuation handling changed. is there a tokenizer compatibility mode?

[02:43] Maya Patel: we surface tokenizer options and a tokenization diagnostic tool in the Console; you'll see where token counts diverge and we recommend prompt rewrites or using our token-normalize preprocessor. for strict parity we can run a tokenization diff against your sample prompts as part of the pilot.

[03:05] Priya Singh: procurement question — do you have a pilot pricing model and contract? our procurement needs to know terms, SOW etc.

[03:12] Jordan Blake: yes — we'll send a pilot pricing sheet. typically pilot is usage-based with a capped monthly commit for a short term (2–4 weeks) and we include support hours. Maya will follow up with estimated GPU capacity for your expected traffic.

[03:25] Samir Rao: security — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integration for keys, audit logs, and data residency options. can Redwood cover those?

[03:33] Jordan Blake: yes — we support SOC2, SAML/Okta, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations. Private deployments allow a control plane in your VPC and on-prem packaging if required. we'll attach the security pack and a sketch of an architecture for VPC/private deployment.

[03:49] Elena Martinez: for private deployments what's the difference between Private and Dedicated? we want data isolation and predictable latency.

[03:56] Maya Patel: Dedicated is reserved capacity hosted in Redwood datacenters/regions with tenant isolation; Private is when you want a customer-managed control plane (VPC or on-prem). Private has more networking setup and is typical for regulated workloads. either way you can pin model versions and rollout policies.

[04:15] Daniel Lee: latency numbers — any real benchmarks for gpt-like workloads vs OpenAI in your tests?

[04:21] Maya Patel: we published latency/cost profiles. i pulled a small benchmark earlier this week: for a 2k context chat prompt we saw median p50 token latency comparable and p95 within a small delta on our Dedicated pools; hosted latency varies by region. we'll run your exact prompt set in the pilot so numbers are apples-to-apples.

[04:40] Jordan Blake: let's walk through a quick parity example — i'll share my screen (note: paraphrasing)

[04:46] Jordan Blake: Example 1: Chat call mapping. OpenAI call: model=gpt-4o, messages=[..], functions=[..], temperature=0.2. Redwood mapping: model=redwood-gpt4o-compatible, chat_messages param is same, function_call behavior supported and we return same type of function invocation object but our field names are sometimes 'tool_call' vs 'function_call' depending on SDK version — we'll include header mappings in the doc.

[05:12] Elena Martinez: that name mismatch worries our engineers — we prefer minimal changes to existing code. how invasive is this SDK change?

[05:19] Maya Patel: our SDKs include a compatibility layer: you can keep your OpenAI-like payloads and set 'compat_mode: openai' to auto-translate names. for Anthropic/Together we have similar mappings. the quickstart repo shows drop-in examples.

[05:38] Samir Rao: streaming — we depend on streaming tokens to render UI progressively. is Redwood streaming identical?

[05:45] Maya Patel: semantics are the same but under the hood we may re-chunk tokens due to batching. most UIs are unaffected, but we recommend you test with your renderer; we also have a streaming toggle to prefer lower latency over throughput.

[06:00] Jordan Blake: now, cost mapping. you have a baseline monthly spend with OpenAI/Anthropic — we'll map expected token costs and show savings opportunities via batching, caching and quantized model suggestions in Optimize.

[06:10] Daniel Lee: what about together.ai models — they have different licensing/throughput behaviors.

[06:15] Maya Patel: for Together and smaller providers we map to equivalent Redwood runtime variants. the main work is ensuring prompts produce consistent outputs — that's where our eval harness helps. we'll run a quality regression test during the pilot on your eval set.

[06:35] Elena Martinez: are there known mismatches with function calling for Anthropic's chat? I remember a previous migration where calls came back as text instead of structured payloads.

[06:44] Maya Patel: sometimes yes — those are usually due to decoding/temperature differences or system prompt handling. we include system-prompt normalization and can pin model seeds/configs to reduce variance. for strict parity we do a guided prompt adapter session with your prompts.

[07:05] Priya Singh: procurement again — SLA? uptime? dedicated customers get SLAs?

[07:10] Jordan Blake: Dedicated customers can get SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; Hosted has best-effort SLAs and quotas. private deployments have contractual uptime clauses. we'll include the SLA summary in the pack.

[07:22] Samir Rao: cool. can we talk about rollout strategy — we want to keep prod on OpenAI for 4 weeks while testing Redwood on a slice of traffic.

[07:29] Maya Patel: recommended is canary routing by route: 5–10% traffic for 1 week, compare latency/cost/quality, then ramp. Redwood Console has built-in rollouts and automatic fallback policies if error rate increases.

[07:43] Jordan Blake: okay quick demo of Console: (narration) Console shows per-route token spend, per-token latency, model profiles, and Optimize suggestions. here's the parity mapping doc link in the Console (we'll send direct link after call).

[08:05] Elena Martinez: last part — monitoring & traces: do you emit tracing hooks we can hook into our observability stack?

[08:12] Maya Patel: yes — we export traces/logs to common sinks, provide token-level breakdown, and have integration templates for DataDog/Prometheus/CloudWatch. audit logs and request-level metadata are available in Private/Dedicated plans with configurable retention.

[08:30] Samir Rao: any gotchas about rate limits and quotas? we have bursty traffic, sometimes thousands of reqs/min.

[08:36] Jordan Blake: we offer burst capacity in Dedicated and have autoscaling; hosted plan has quotas but you can request quota increases. for very bursty workloads we recommend Dedicated with burst pool.

[08:50] Daniel Lee: are there examples of customers who migrated from Anthropic and kept prediction parity?

[08:56] Maya Patel: yes, a few health-tech customers. we typically run a small re-eval of prompts, adjust system prompts, and sometimes apply a light post-processing step. results are in the case study we'll share (link in pack).

[09:10] Jordan Blake: want to confirm next steps: Jordan will send parity mapping doc + quickstart repo + pricing sheet + security pack; Elena will share prompt set and traffic profile; Maya will schedule pilot kickoff and run benchmarks; Priya will circulate procurement questions.

[09:25] Elena Martinez: sounds good. any other questions?

[09:29] Samir Rao: none from me. thanks, this was helpful.

[09:32] Jordan Blake: awesome — we'll follow up by tomorrow with the docs. thanks everyone.

[09:36] (call ends)

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-heard words and small speaker attribution glitches due to auto-transcription. The transcript intentionally retains some imperfection: e.g., "Redbend Console" and minor grammar drops. Pilot plan: 2-week benchmark comparing latency, p95, cost-per-1k-tokens and quality regressions using NovaHealth's sample prompt/eval set.
